primary.question: Do MSAS and CSEE Masters students face the same dissertation requirements?
primary.expected_answer: No. For MSAS dissertation modules (MA981/MA983) students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in the interview component AND 50 in the written report in order to pass the module and gain the credits - a two-component requirement. The CSEE accredited Masters rules do not impose that split interview/report requirement; CSEE's rules concern the accredited programme list and the non-accredited exit award titles.
primary.actual_answer:
Both schools require a dual pass mark for the dissertation/project element, but the specifics differ:

**MSAS (School of Mathematics, Statistics and Actuarial Science):** For dissertation modules (e.g., on MSc Data Science, MSc Applied Data Science, MSc Data Science with Professional Placement, MSc Data Science and its Applications, and other MSc courses listed for 2025-26), students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in the interview component **and** 50 in the written report to pass the module and gain the credits. (https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/mscs-in-school-maths-statistics-actuarial-science-25.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2024-25/department-specific/pg-roa-jan-start-mscs-school-of-mathsstatisticsactuarial-sci-24.pdf)

**CSEE:** For accredited MSc Project and Dissertation courses, students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in the Project Demonstration Oral (PDO) **and** 50 in the written Dissertation element to pass the module and achieve the credits — the same dual-component structure, but the components are named differently (PDO rather than "interview") and it is framed within CSEE's broader accredited Masters award rules (180 credits attempted, 160 passed, core modules and dissertation must be passed, condonement rules for up to 20 non-core credits, etc.). (https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-full-time-accredited-degrees---jan-start.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-ft-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-pt-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2024-25/department-specific/csee_model_1_accredited_january_starts_rules_jan25.pdf)

**In short:** The underlying principle — a mandatory 50 pass mark in each of two dissertation components — is the same for both schools, but the CSEE documents also spell out much more detailed award-eligibility rules (credit totals, condonement, resubmission conditions, Merit/Distinction thresholds) that aren't mirrored in the MSAS excerpts I have. It's possible MSAS has equivalent broader award-eligibility rules elsewhere in its Rules of Assessment documents, but they are not included in what I can see here, so I can't confirm whether MSAS's overall eligibility criteria match CSEE's exactly.

follow_up.question: What happens to a CSEE student who doesn't meet the accredited award requirements?
follow_up.expected_answer: They may be considered for a non-accredited exit award instead - titled MSc Computing for students originally enrolled on Advanced Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Text Analytics or Computer Games, and MSc Computer Systems Engineering for students on 5G and Emerging Communication Systems, Computer Engineering, Computer Networks and Security, Electronic Engineering or Intelligent Systems and Robotics.
follow_up.actual_answer:
A CSEE student who doesn't meet the requirements for an accredited Masters award will be considered by the Board of Examiners for a **non-accredited Masters exit award** instead, provided they meet these criteria:

- **Credits:** Must have attempted 180 credits at Masters Level (Level 7), of which 140 must be passed, with the remaining credits condoned (subject to the condonement condition below).
- **Core modules and dissertation:** Must pass all taught core modules and the dissertation (or equivalent) — this cannot be condoned.
- **Condonement of non-core failures:** Failure with a mark of 40 or more in up to 40 credits of non-core taught modules may be condoned, provided the overall weighted average for all taught modules is 50 or more.
- The 2024-25 rules also specify passing at least 60 taught module credits at the first attempt, unless there are substantiated extenuating circumstances accepted by the Board.

**Merit/Distinction:** This non-accredited award can still be passed with Merit or Distinction, using the same overall weighted average thresholds as the accredited award (60+ for Merit, 70+ for Distinction).

**Title:** The non-accredited award carries a different title from the accredited one — for example, students originally enrolled on the accredited "MSc Artificial Intelligence" would receive the non-accredited exit award title "MSc Computing."

**If a student was transferred onto a non-accredited course but still doesn't meet even these requirements**, the Board will consider them for a non-accredited exit award under their new course title, following the same criteria.

**Reassessment:** Separately, students who fail a taught module get one opportunity for reassessment (in the 2025-26 rules) or, under the 2024-25 rules, may attempt reassessment in failed modules up to a maximum of 60 taught module credits. No second attempt is allowed before the Board of Examiners confirms marks, and a reassessment mark is normally capped at 50 unless extenuating circumstances are accepted.

Sources: https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-full-time-accredited-degrees---jan-start.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2024-25/department-specific/csee_model_1_accredited_january_starts_rules_jan25.pdf; https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-pt-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf

primary.question: Is the pass mark and condonement rule the same for SRES and East 15 Masters students?
primary.expected_answer: Yes, on both points. For SRES and for East 15 the pass mark for all Masters modules is 50, credits are only awarded if the module is passed, and where failure with a mark of 40 is condoned the credits are not awarded. Core modules must be passed with no condonement of marks below a pass allowed in both.
primary.actual_answer:
Yes, the core rules are essentially the same for both the School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Science (SRES) and East 15 Acting School Masters students (2025-26):

- **Pass mark**: 50 for all modules in both cases. Credits are only awarded if a module is passed; if a fail mark of 40 is condoned, no credits are awarded for that module.
- **Condonement**: In both cases, to pass the Masters a student must attempt 180 credits at Level 7, of which 140 must be passed, with the remaining credits condoned. Failure with a mark of 40 or more, for up to 40 credits in non-core taught modules, may be condoned provided the overall weighted average for all taught modules is 50.
- **Core modules and dissertation**: In both, core modules and the dissertation (or equivalent) must be passed outright, with no condonement allowed below the pass mark.

One additional SRES-specific requirement not mentioned for East 15 is that SRES students must also pass all placement/work-based assessments.

primary.question: How are placements and practice-based modules assessed in HSC and SRES programmes?
primary.expected_answer: In the HSC MSc Occupational Therapy, placements are marked on a pass/fail basis rather than with a numerical mark. In SRES, certain modules require students to pass all module assignments in addition to passing the module overall - for example HS632 Preparation for Independent and Supplementary Prescribing V300 (NMC/HCPC) and the musculoskeletal ultrasound modules SE708, SE709 and SE710.
primary.actual_answer:
Placements and practice-based modules are consistently treated as pass/fail, credit-bearing assessments across these programmes, though the specific rules differ slightly by programme type:

**Undergraduate 3-year and 4-year Honours Degree placements** (Years 1, 2 and 3 variations documents; department not specified but covering practice-based learning placements generally):
- The practice-based learning placement element of all placement modules is assessed as pass/fail only.
- Students must pass all practice-based learning placements.
- Students get only two attempts at the placement element (compared with three attempts for other module assessments).
- If a student fails a placement, they must undertake and pass a full repeat placement in the same clinical specialty, normally as the next scheduled placement subject to capacity.
- Failing a placement on reassessment, or failing two placements at first attempt, leads to required withdrawal from the programme, unless the Board of Examiners accepts valid Extenuating Circumstances.
- Students may trail no more than one practice-based learning placement into the subsequent level.
- Resubmission marks are capped: if the pre-resubmission Module Aggregate was under the Pass Mark, it can only be improved up to the Pass Mark.

**MSci Nursing (Health and Social Care, 2024-25 and 2025-26)**:
- "Person-Centred Care" modules are assessed via a Practice Assessment Document (PAD) and a Drug Calculations Exam; these are credit-bearing but ungraded, awarded pass/fail only.
- Progression also requires a minimum 90% mark in the Drug Calculation Exam component of module HS187, and students must pass all "Professional Values in Practice" placement elements for HS187 to be trailed into Year Three.

**SRES Modular programmes (School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Science, 2025-26)**:
- All work placement/work-based assessments are assessed on a pass/fail basis. They are non-credit-bearing but must be passed.
- Certain named modules (e.g., HS632, various SE-coded ultrasound and musculoskeletal modules) additionally require students to pass all individual module assignments, not just the overall module mark.

follow_up.question: Does either lead to professional registration?
follow_up.expected_answer: Yes. Successful completion of the HSC MSc Occupational Therapy leads to eligibility to apply for registration with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). The SRES prescribing module is likewise tied to NMC/HCPC professional requirements.
follow_up.actual_answer:
Based on what's visible here, only the MSc OT programme and the SRES musculoskeletal/prescribing modules give clear signals on professional registration:

- **MSc OT (Health and Social Care, 2025-26)**: This is described as a "pre-registration programme," and placement failure rules explicitly reference withdrawal from "a pre-registration programme" and fitness to practise concerns — indicating this programme does lead to professional registration (as an Occupational Therapist).

- **SRES Modular programmes (School of Sport, Rehabilitation and Exercise Science, 2025-26)**: The module HS632 is named "Preparation for Independent and Supplementary Prescribing V300 (NMC/HCPC)" — explicitly tied to Nursing and Midwifery Council/Health and Care Professions Council registration/regulation. So: yes, both the MSc OT and the SRES musculoskeletal/prescribing-related programmes connect to professional registration (HCPC and/or NMC), though the Postgraduate Diploma variant in SRES does not.

primary.question: For HSC and Psychology Masters programmes, what is the pass mark and how is progression handled?
primary.expected_answer: In both, the pass mark for all modules of the Masters degree is 50, credits are only awarded if the module is passed, and failure with a mark of 40 may be condoned without credits being awarded. In the HSC MSc Occupational Therapy students may progress to Year 2 while trailing a maximum of 30 credits.
primary.actual_answer:
## Health and Social Care (HSC) Masters Programmes

**MSc Periodontology** (2025-26):
- Pass mark for all modules is **50**. Credits are only awarded if the module is passed. If a failure with a mark of 40 is condoned, the credits are still not awarded, though the mark counts toward the overall weighted average.
- Taught module averages and dissertation marks are rounded to the nearest whole number (e.g., 49.5 rounds to 50, 49.4 rounds to 49).
- **Progression**: Students may progress to Year 2 or Year 3 while trailing a maximum of 30 credits, meaning they carry forward reassessment in up to 30 credits and complete it at the earliest opportunity offered by the School in the following year. An in-year Board of Examiners meeting may be convened.

**MSc Advanced Clinical Practitioner Apprenticeship / Leadership in Health and Care / HS632 modules** (2025-26):
- For Leadership in Health and Care, progression is based on **passing all core modules**.
- For HS632, specific components have distinct pass marks: the Pharmacology Examination requires a mark of **80** to pass, and the Numeracy Examination requires a mark of **100** to pass. Failed HS632 work is normally resubmitted within four weeks of students receiving marked work.
- Progression for HS632 is handled **between modules rather than by levels or stages**.
- Note: students on the Apprenticeship route are not eligible for a Postgraduate Certificate exit award, though a transfer request to PG Cert Health Care Practice can be made.

## Psychology Masters Programmes

For the **MSc Psychology (C800 JS)**, part-time Model 2 January starts and related January-start Masters rules (2024-25/2025-26):
- Pass mark for all modules is **50**. Credits are only awarded if the module is passed; if a failure with a mark of 40 is condoned, credits are still not awarded.
- Taught module averages and dissertation marks are rounded to the nearest whole number as above.
- **Progression to Year Two**: Students may still progress even if they failed modules in Year One following a reassessment attempt. However, they will no longer be on track for the Masters degree if further reassessment attempts cannot be offered due to a lack of accepted extenuating circumstances. In certain scenarios, students may only proceed if still eligible for an exit award (Postgraduate Diploma or Postgraduate Certificate).
- To be awarded a **Postgraduate Certificate**: attempt 60 credits at Level 7, of which at least 40 must be passed (remaining credits condoned); pass all taught core modules; pass 15 credits at the first attempt unless extenuating circumstances are accepted; failure with a mark of 40+ for up to 20 credits in non-core modules may be condoned.
- Merit requires an overall weighted average of 60+ across 120 PG Diploma credits; Distinction requires 70+.

Both HSC and Psychology programmes therefore share the standard Masters pass mark of 50, with condoned fails at 40 not earning credit, though HSC has additional programme-specific rules (e.g., HS632's stricter marks and module-based progression) not seen in the Psychology documents.

**Sources:**

- https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/mscperiodontology_25.pdf

primary.question: Which of MSAS, Psychology and CSEE have programme-specific dissertation rules that differ from the standard Masters rules?
primary.expected_answer: MSAS does: its dissertation modules MA981/MA983 require a pass mark of 50 in the interview component and 50 in the written report separately. The Psychology MSc rules follow the standard Masters pattern (pass mark 50 for all modules, condonement at 40). The CSEE rules concern accredited programme lists and non-accredited exit award titles rather than a distinct dissertation requirement.
primary.actual_answer:
All three have department-specific dissertation rules layered on top of the standard Masters framework, though the nature of the variation differs:

- **School of Mathematics, Statistics and Actuarial Science (MSAS)**: For Dissertation modules (MA981/MA983) on its MSc courses, students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in **both** the interview component and the written report in order to pass the module and gain the credits — a dual-component pass requirement beyond a single overall module mark ([mscs-in-school-maths-statistics-actuarial-science-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/mscs-in-school-maths-statistics-actuarial-science-25.pdf); also confirmed for the January-start courses in the 2024-25 variation).

- **CSEE**: For the MSc Project and Dissertation, students must achieve a pass mark of 50 in **both** the Project Demonstration Oral (PDO) and the written Dissertation element to pass the module and gain credits — the same dual-component structure as MSAS, applied across full-time and part-time accredited Masters and the non-accredited January-start MSc Artificial Intelligence and its Applications ([csee-ft-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-ft-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf); [csee-pt-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-pt-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf); [csee_non_accredited_january_start_2025_msc.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2024-25/department-specific/csee_non_accredited_january_start_2025_msc.pdf)).

- **Psychology (MSc Psychology, part-time January start)**: The excerpts I have show only the standard Masters rules — pass mark of 50 for all modules, and the standard treatment of the dissertation for Postgraduate Diploma/Certificate exit awards (dissertation credits can count toward a PG Diploma but not a PG Certificate). There is no indication of a special dual-component or otherwise varied dissertation pass requirement for Psychology in what I can see ([pgt-part-time-model-2-january-starts-rules-of-assessment-jan-25-start.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2024-25/masters-taught-courses/pgt-part-time-model-2-january-starts-rules-of-assessment-jan-25-start.pdf)).

**Summary**: MSAS and CSEE both have explicit programme-specific dissertation rules requiring separate pass marks of 50 in two distinct components (interview/written report for MSAS; PDO/written dissertation for CSEE), which differ from the standard single-mark approach. For Psychology, the documents I can see don't show any such variation — only the standard Masters dissertation/exit-award rules.
